claims.text: Conventional strengthening of polycrystalline metals or alloys typically comes at the cost of reduced ductility.
A machine-learning model can identify an optimized conventional-processing window.
The optimized processing window can produce controlled grain refinement.
The optimized processing window can produce a uniform precipitate distribution.
Machine-learning-guided optimization of conventional processing can enhance both strength and ductility.
Processing temperature, strain rate, and composition can be used as model inputs linked to microstructural outcomes.
The proposed processing remains within conventional processing methods.
An optimized grain structure and uniform precipitate distribution improve load transfer.
An optimized grain structure and uniform precipitate distribution increase resistance to crack initiation.
The machine-learning model can identify non-intuitive interactions among processing variables.
The identified processing-variable interactions lead to fine grains.
The identified processing-variable interactions lead to well-dispersed precipitates.
The resulting microstructure enhances dislocation motion.
The resulting microstructure improves load distribution.
The resulting microstructure improves strength without severely compromising ductility.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will increase yield strength relative to conventional processing.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will increase ultimate tensile strength relative to conventional processing.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will retain ductility or cause only a minor ductility reduction relative to conventional processing.
The approach does not introduce entirely new material phases or use extreme processing environments.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that both strength and ductility are enhanced, whereas the predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be retained or even slightly reduced.

The predicted outcome permits retained or slightly reduced ductility, but the falsification rule requires statistically significant improvement in both strength and ductility; an outcome allowed by the prediction could therefore be classified as falsification.

The design distinguishes standard and ML-optimized processing conditions but then says both sets should receive the same processing conditions; this is internally ambiguous unless it means only non-intervention conditions are held constant.
